children: European equity markets were poised to open little changed on Wednesday as investors assessed dovish signals from a Federal Reserve official while awaiting key US inflation data.
New York Fed President John Williams indicated that one additional rate hike may be warranted this year, but further monetary tightening would likely be unnecessary in 2027.
In Europe, attention will turn to German wholesale prices and Spanish consumer inflation figures, alongside further remarks from ECB President Christine Lagarde.
On Tuesday, Lagarde noted that elevated euro-area inflation, driven by rising energy prices, had yet to spread to the broader economy.
In corporate news, Dutch chipmaker ASML said it would be unable to fully meet demand over the next two years, raising further concerns about the sustainability of the AI investment boom.
In premarket trading, Euro Stoxx 50 futures hovered around the flatline.

title: European Stocks Set for a Flat Opening
